- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.75) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (e.g., <0.2) and forecast is overly conservative, slightly increase the mean to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Model tends to overestimate early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile — apply a 2–3% downward bias to first 5–7 days.  
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model often fails to adjust — add a 1–2% upward bias to forecasted mean.  
- When sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from +0.9 to -0.5), model often lags — adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.  
- Avoid over-relying on recent 3-day highs — if sentiment is neutral or mixed, use 7-day moving average for smoothing.
